rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_account_transactions AS (
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  rowid AS transaction_id,
  txn_date AS transaction_date,
  txn_amount AS amount
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND txn_date IS NOT NULL
  AND txn_amount IS NOT NULL
),
customer_monthly_aggregates AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(ct.txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  -- compute month_end by taking first day of next month minus one day: use YYYY-MM trick
  date(substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) || '-01', '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
  substr(ct.txn_date, 1, 4) || '-' || substr(ct.txn_date, 6, 2) AS month_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount WHEN ct.txn_type = 'credit' THEN ct.txn_amount WHEN ct.txn_type = 'refund' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END)
    - SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN ct.txn_amount WHEN ct.txn_type = 'debit' THEN ct.txn_amount WHEN ct.txn_type = 'charge' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END)
    AS monthly_net_amount,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type IN ('deposit','credit','refund') THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_credit_total,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type IN ('withdrawal','debit','charge') THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_debit_total
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_start
),
calendar_months AS (
SELECT
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_txn)) AS month_start,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_txn), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
  strftime('%m-%Y', date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', min_txn))) AS month_year
FROM (
  SELECT
    (SELECT MIN(transaction_date) FROM customer_account_transactions) AS min_txn,
    (SELECT MAX(transaction_date) FROM customer_account_transactions) AS max_txn
)
UNION ALL
SELECT
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(min_txn, '+' || n || ' months'))) AS month_start,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(min_txn, '+' || n || ' months')), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
  strftime('%m-%Y', date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(min_txn, '+' || n || ' months')))) AS month_year
FROM (
  SELECT
    (SELECT MIN(transaction_date) FROM customer_account_transactions) AS min_txn,
    (SELECT MAX(transaction_date) FROM customer_account_transactions) AS max_txn,
    (j.n) AS n
  FROM (
    SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11
    UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17
    UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23
    UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
    UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
    UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41
    UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47
    UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53
    UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
  ) AS j
  WHERE date(min_txn, '+' || j.n || ' months') <= max_txn
)
),
customer_monthly_running_balance AS (
SELECT
  a.customer_id,
  m.month_start,
  m.month_end,
  m.month_year,
  COALESCE(agg.monthly_net_amount, 0) AS monthly_net_amount,
  -- running cumulative sum of monthly_net_amount over months per customer up to current month_end
  (
    SELECT SUM(COALESCE(a2.monthly_net_amount, 0))
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates a2
    WHERE a2.customer_id = a.customer_id
      AND a2.month_start <= m.month_start
  ) AS month_end_balance,
  -- change from previous month: current month net minus previous month net
  COALESCE(COALESCE(agg.monthly_net_amount, 0) - (
    SELECT COALESCE(a3.monthly_net_amount, 0)
    FROM customer_monthly_aggregates a3
    WHERE a3.customer_id = a.customer_id
      AND a3.month_start = (
        SELECT month_start
        FROM calendar_months cm_prev
        WHERE cm_prev.month_end < m.month_start
        ORDER BY cm_prev.month_end DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )
  ), COALESCE(agg.monthly_net_amount, 0)) AS monthly_change
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_monthly_aggregates) a
CROSS JOIN
  calendar_months m
LEFT JOIN
  customer_monthly_aggregates agg
  ON agg.customer_id = a.customer_id
  AND agg.month_start = m.month_start
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  m.month_start,
  m.month_end,
  m.month_year,
  COALESCE(a.monthly_net_amount, 0) AS monthly_net_amount,
  COALESCE(a.monthly_credit_total, 0) AS monthly_credit_total,
  COALESCE(a.monthly_debit_total, 0) AS monthly_debit_total,
  COALESCE(r.month_end_balance, 0) AS month_end_balance,
  COALESCE(r.monthly_change, 0) AS monthly_change
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_account_transactions) c
CROSS JOIN
  calendar_months m
LEFT JOIN
  customer_monthly_aggregates a
  ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id
  AND a.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN
  customer_monthly_running_balance r
  ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
  AND r.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY
  c.customer_id,
  m.month_start

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_monthly_balances AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS yyyymm,
    SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) -
    SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_balance
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y', txn_date), strftime('%m', txn_date)
),
all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
all_2020_months AS (
  -- derive months that actually appear in 2020 in the data; fallback to any sample date in 2020 present
  SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS yyyymm,
         CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
         CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS month
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE strftime('%Y', txn_date) = '2020'
),
monthly_customer_balance_matrix AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    m.year,
    m.month,
    m.yyyymm,
    COALESCE(b.month_balance, 0) AS month_balance
  FROM all_customers c
  CROSS JOIN all_2020_months m
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balances b
    ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id AND m.year = b.year AND m.month = b.month
),
monthly_stats_2020 AS (
  SELECT
    yyyymm,
    SUM(CASE WHEN month_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
    AVG(month_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM monthly_customer_balance_matrix
  GROUP BY yyyymm
)
SELECT
  high.yyyymm AS highest_count_month,
  high.positive_count AS highest_count_customers,
  high.avg_balance AS highest_month_avg_balance,
  low.yyyymm AS lowest_count_month,
  low.positive_count AS lowest_count_customers,
  low.avg_balance AS lowest_month_avg_balance,
  (high.avg_balance - low.avg_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (SELECT yyyymm, positive_count, avg_balance FROM monthly_stats_2020 ORDER BY positive_count DESC, yyyymm ASC LIMIT 1) AS high,
  (SELECT yyyymm, positive_count, avg_balance FROM monthly_stats_2020 ORDER BY positive_count ASC, yyyymm ASC LIMIT 1) AS low

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cust_monthly_closing_balance AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(ct.txn_date, 1, 7) AS month_date,
  SUM(
    CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
         WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
         ELSE ct.txn_amount
    END
  ) AS monthly_net,
  SUM(
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
           WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
           ELSE ct.txn_amount
      END
    )
  ) OVER (PARTITION BY ct.customer_id ORDER BY substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, substr(ct.txn_date,1,7)
),
all_customers AS (
SELECT DISTINCT
  customer_id
FROM
  customer_transactions
),
cust_txn_monthly_net AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
           WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
           ELSE 0 END) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_type IN ('deposit', 'withdrawal')
GROUP BY customer_id, month_date
),
cust_most_recent_month AS (
SELECT
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  m.most_recent_month_date AS most_recent_month_date,
  m.closing_balance AS closing_balance_most_recent,
  p.closing_balance AS closing_balance_previous
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      month_date AS most_recent_month_date,
      closing_balance,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_date DESC) AS rn
    FROM cust_monthly_closing_balance
  ) m
LEFT JOIN cust_monthly_closing_balance p
  ON m.customer_id = p.customer_id
  AND p.month_date = (
    SELECT MAX(month_date) FROM cust_monthly_closing_balance p2
    WHERE p2.customer_id = m.customer_id
      AND p2.month_date < m.most_recent_month_date
  )
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM cust_monthly_closing_balance
) c ON m.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE m.rn = 1
)
SELECT
  COUNT(all_customers.customer_id) AS total_customers_with_transactions,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN (cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous IS NULL OR cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous = 0)
        THEN CASE WHEN (cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_most_recent * 100) > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
      ELSE CASE WHEN ((cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_most_recent - cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous) * 1.0 / cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous) > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
    END
  ) AS customers_with_recent_growth_gt_5pct,
  100.0 * SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN (cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous IS NULL OR cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous = 0)
        THEN CASE WHEN (cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_most_recent * 100) > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
      ELSE CASE WHEN ((cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_most_recent - cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous) * 1.0 / cust_most_recent_month.closing_balance_previous) > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
    END
  ) / COUNT(all_customers.customer_id) AS percent_customers_with_recent_growth_gt_5pct
FROM all_customers
LEFT JOIN cust_most_recent_month USING (customer_id)

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH months_in_transactions AS (
SELECT
  strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS year_month,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date)) AS month_start_date,
  (strftime('%Y', txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', txn_date)) AS month_index
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY year_month, month_start_date, month_index
),
non_negative_customer_balance_by_month_start AS (
SELECT
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(mc.month_start,1,7) AS month,
  mc.month_start AS first_day_of_month,
  CASE
    WHEN IFNULL((
      SELECT SUM(txn_amount)
      FROM customer_transactions t
      WHERE t.customer_id = c.customer_id
        AND date(t.txn_date) < date(mc.month_start)
    ),0) < 0 THEN 0
    ELSE IFNULL((
      SELECT SUM(txn_amount)
      FROM customer_transactions t2
      WHERE t2.customer_id = c.customer_id
        AND date(t2.txn_date) < date(mc.month_start)
    ),0)
  END AS balance_non_negative
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c
  CROSS JOIN (
    -- generate month starts covered by transactions: first day of each month present in data and one month after last txn month is unnecessary
    SELECT DISTINCT date(substr(txn_date,1,8) || '01') AS month_start
    FROM customer_transactions
  ) mc
),
customer_transaction_dates AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- canonicalize txn_date to YYYY-MM-DD using date() to handle common formats; keep original text if invalid yields NULL
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  -- derive year_month as YYYY-MM from canonicalized date; if date() is NULL, attempt substr of original as fallback
  CASE
    WHEN date(txn_date) IS NOT NULL THEN strftime('%Y-%m', date(txn_date))
    WHEN length(txn_date) >= 7 THEN substr(txn_date,1,7)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS year_month,
  txn_amount AS amount
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_cumulative_balance_as_of_date AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  ct.txn_date AS cutoff_date,
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(t2.txn_amount), 0)
   FROM customer_transactions t2
   WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
     AND t2.txn_date <= ct.txn_date
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM customer_transactions ct
)
SELECT
  m.year_month AS month,
  SUM(n.balance_non_negative) AS total_balance_prev_month
FROM months_in_transactions m
JOIN non_negative_customer_balance_by_month_start n
  ON m.year_month = n.month
WHERE m.month_index > (SELECT MIN(month_index) FROM months_in_transactions)
GROUP BY m.year_month
ORDER BY m.year_month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH normalized_customer_transactions AS (
SELECT
  rowid AS transaction_id,
  customer_id,
  DATE(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  LOWER(txn_type) AS txn_type,
  CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC) AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_daily_transaction_totals AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  SUM(
    CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END
  ) AS net_txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id AS customer_id,
  d.txn_date AS calendar_date,
  AVG(d.end_of_day_balance) OVER (
    PARTITION BY d.customer_id
    ORDER BY d.txn_date
    ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS rolling_30d_avg_balance
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    -- derive end_of_day_balance by cumulative sum of net transactions up to and including that date
    SUM(txn_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS end_of_day_balance
  FROM (
    -- take daily net transaction totals per customer/date
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      txn_date,
      SUM(COALESCE(txn_amount,0) * CASE WHEN txn_type IN ('deposit','DEPOSIT','credit','CREDIT','CR') THEN 1
                                        WHEN txn_type IN ('withdrawal','WITHDRAWAL','debit','DEBIT','DR') THEN -1
                                        ELSE 0 END) AS txn_net
    FROM normalized_customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
  ) daily_net
) d
-- ensure only dates where at least 30 days of history exist ending on that date by requiring the window to be full:
WHERE (
  SELECT COUNT(1)
  FROM (
    SELECT 1
    FROM (
      -- count distinct prior dates for same customer up to current date inclusive
      SELECT DISTINCT txn_date
      FROM normalized_customer_transactions t2
      WHERE t2.customer_id = d.customer_id
        AND t2.txn_date <= d.txn_date
    )
  )
) >= 30
),
customer_monthly_max_30day_avg AS (
SELECT
  r.customer_id,
  substr(r.calendar_date,1,7) AS month,
  -- month_start_date: first day of the calendar month containing the calendar_date
  (substr(r.calendar_date,1,7) || '-01') AS month_start_date,
  -- maximum raw 30-day rolling average balance for this customer within the calendar month
  MAX(r.rolling_30d_avg_balance) AS max_30d_avg_balance_in_month,
  -- baseline_month: the customer's baseline month (defined as the month of their earliest rolling-date in this dataset)
  substr(min(r.calendar_date) OVER (PARTITION BY r.customer_id),1,7) AS baseline_month
FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance AS r
GROUP BY r.customer_id, substr(r.calendar_date,1,7)
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN max_30d_avg_balance_in_month < 0 THEN 0 ELSE max_30d_avg_balance_in_month END) AS monthly_sum_of_customers_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM customer_monthly_max_30day_avg
WHERE month <> baseline_month
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs. Only consider overs that had the most runs conceded within their respective matches, and among these, determine which bowlers conceded the most runs in a single over overall.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH over_level_runs AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(b.runs_scored), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(e.extra_runs), 0) AS runs_conceded_in_over
FROM batsman_scored b
LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
),
over_bowler_map AS (
SELECT
  match_id,
  innings_no,
  over_id,
  bowler
FROM
  ball_by_ball
WHERE
  bowler IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  match_id,
  innings_no,
  over_id,
  bowler
),
player_dim AS (
SELECT
  player.player_id AS player_id,
  player.player_name AS player_name
FROM player
),
match_max_over_runs AS (
SELECT
  olr.match_id,
  MAX(olr.runs_conceded_in_over) AS max_runs_in_any_over
FROM
  over_level_runs olr
GROUP BY
  olr.match_id
)
SELECT
  P.player_id,
  P.player_name,
  OL.match_id,
  OL.over_id,
  OL.runs_conceded_in_over,
  OL.innings_no
FROM over_level_runs OL
JOIN match_max_over_runs M
  ON OL.match_id = M.match_id
  AND OL.runs_conceded_in_over = M.max_runs_in_any_over
JOIN over_bowler_map OB
  ON OL.match_id = OB.match_id
  AND OL.innings_no = OB.innings_no
  AND OL.over_id = OB.over_id
JOIN player_dim P
  ON OB.bowler = P.player_id
ORDER BY OL.runs_conceded_in_over DESC, OL.match_id ASC
LIMIT 3

rows.question: Which bowler has the lowest bowling average per wicket taken?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH delivery_level_wickets AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.bowler,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out AS wicket_type
FROM wicket_taken w
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND b.bowler IS NOT NULL
  AND w.player_out IS NOT NULL
),
player_basic AS (
SELECT
  player.player_id AS player_id,
  player.player_name AS player_name
FROM player
),
delivery_level_balls AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.bowler,
  bs.runs_scored AS batsman_runs,
  er.extra_runs AS extra_runs
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
),
bowler_aggregates AS (
SELECT
  d.bowler AS bowler_id,
  SUM(d.batsman_runs + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs_conceded,
  COALESCE(w.wicket_count, 0) AS wickets_taken
FROM
  delivery_level_balls d
LEFT JOIN
  extra_runs e
  ON d.match_id = e.match_id
  AND d.innings_no = e.innings_no
  AND d.over_id = e.over_id
  AND d.ball_id = e.ball_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings_no,
    over_id,
    ball_id,
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS wicket_count
  FROM
    delivery_level_wickets
  GROUP BY
    match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id, bowler
) w
  ON d.match_id = w.match_id
  AND d.innings_no = w.innings_no
  AND d.over_id = w.over_id
  AND d.ball_id = w.ball_id
  AND d.bowler = w.bowler
GROUP BY
  d.bowler
)
SELECT
  b.bowler_id AS player_id,
  p.player_name,
  b.total_runs_conceded,
  b.wickets_taken,
  (b.total_runs_conceded * 1.0) / b.wickets_taken AS bowling_average
FROM bowler_aggregates b
JOIN player_basic p
  ON b.bowler_id = p.player_id
WHERE b.wickets_taken > 0

rows.question: Please examine our database records for Chinese cities (country_code_2 = 'cn') during July 2021 and identify both the shortest and longest streaks of consecutive date entries. For each date in these streaks, return exactly one record per date along with the corresponding city name. In your output, please ensure the first letter of each city name is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Display the dates and city names for both the shortest and longest consecutive date streaks, ordered by date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cn_july AS (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    city_name,
    trim(insert_date) AS insert_date
  FROM cities
  WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
    AND substr(trim(insert_date),6,2) = '07'  -- July
),
-- Choose one record per date (lowest city_id)
one_per_day AS (
  SELECT
    cj.insert_date,
    cj.city_id,
    cj.city_name
  FROM cn_july cj
  JOIN (
    SELECT insert_date, MIN(city_id) AS city_id
    FROM cn_july
    GROUP BY insert_date
  ) m ON cj.insert_date = m.insert_date AND cj.city_id = m.city_id
),
-- order dates and compute gaps to detect consecutive runs
ordered AS (
  SELECT
    insert_date,
    city_id,
    city_name,
    DATE(insert_date) AS d,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY DATE(insert_date)) AS rn
  FROM one_per_day
),
-- grouping trick: date minus row_number gives constant for consecutive sequences
groups AS (
  SELECT
    insert_date,
    city_id,
    city_name,
    d,
    rn,
    DATE(d, printf('-%d day', rn)) AS grp_key
  FROM ordered
),
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    grp_key,
    MIN(d) AS start_date,
    MAX(d) AS end_date,
    COUNT(*) AS length
  FROM groups
  GROUP BY grp_key
),
-- find min and max streak lengths within July (there will be at least one row)
agg AS (
  SELECT MIN(length) AS min_len, MAX(length) AS max_len FROM streaks
),
-- pick streaks that match shortest or longest
selected_streaks AS (
  SELECT s.*, a.min_len, a.max_len
  FROM streaks s CROSS JOIN agg a
  WHERE s.length = a.min_len OR s.length = a.max_len
),
-- expand selected streaks back to individual dates and city names
result AS (
  SELECT
    g.insert_date AS date,
    -- Normalize city name: first letter uppercase, rest lowercase
    UPPER(SUBSTR(g.city_name,1,1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(g.city_name,2)) AS city_name,
    CASE WHEN s.length = s.min_len THEN 'shortest' ELSE 'longest' END AS streak_type,
    s.length
  FROM groups g
  JOIN selected_streaks s
    ON DATE(g.d) BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date
)
SELECT date, city_name, streak_type
FROM result
ORDER BY streak_type, DATE(date)

rows.question: Could you review our records in June 2022 and identify which countries have the longest streak of consecutive inserted city dates? Please list the 2-letter length country codes of these countries.

WITH june_days AS (

  SELECT city_id, country_code_2, date(substr(insert_date,1,10)) AS day_date

),
country_day AS (

  FROM june_days
  GROUP BY country_code_2, day_date
),
numbered AS (

    day_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code_2 ORDER BY day_date) AS rn
  FROM country_day
),
islands AS (
  -- gap-and-island trick: day_date minus row_number (as days) gives same value for consecutive dates
  SELECT
    country_code_2,
    day_date,
    rn,
    DATE(day_date, printf('-%d days', rn)) AS grp
  FROM numbered
),
country_runs AS (
  -- group by country and grp to compute consecutive-run lengths

    country_code_2,

FROM country_max_run
WHERE max_streak_length = (SELECT MAX(max_streak_length) FROM country_max_run)

rows.question: Calculate the number of new cities inserted in April, May, and June for each year from 2021 to 2023. For each month, compute the cumulative running total of cities added for that specific month across the years up to and including the given year (i.e., sum the counts of that month over the years). Additionally, calculate the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total for each month, comparing each year to the previous year. Present the results only for 2022 and 2023, listing the year, the month, the total number of cities added in that month, the cumulative running total for that month, and the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total. Use the data from 2021 solely as a baseline for calculating growth rates, and exclude it from the final output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cities_date_parts AS (
SELECT
  city_id AS city_id,
  insert_date AS insert_date,
  CAST(substr(insert_date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(substr(insert_date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  CASE CAST(substr(insert_date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN 1 THEN 'January'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'February'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'March'
    WHEN 4 THEN 'April'
    WHEN 5 THEN 'May'
    WHEN 6 THEN 'June'
    WHEN 7 THEN 'July'
    WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
    WHEN 9 THEN 'September'
    WHEN 10 THEN 'October'
    WHEN 11 THEN 'November'
    WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS month_name
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
),
monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS (
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  CASE CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
    WHEN 1 THEN 'January' WHEN 2 THEN 'February' WHEN 3 THEN 'March' WHEN 4 THEN 'April'
    WHEN 5 THEN 'May' WHEN 6 THEN 'June' WHEN 7 THEN 'July' WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
    WHEN 9 THEN 'September' WHEN 10 THEN 'October' WHEN 11 THEN 'November' WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
    ELSE NULL END AS month_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT city_id) AS monthly_total
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
),
cities_filtered_by_date_range AS (
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date
FROM
  cities
WHERE
  insert_date IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) IN (2021, 2022, 2023)
),
monthly_running_totals_and_yoy_inputs AS (
SELECT
  m.year AS year,
  m.month AS month,
  m.month_name AS month_name,
  m.monthly_total AS monthly_total,
  -- running_total: cumulative sum of monthly_total ordered by year then month
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS m2
   WHERE m2.year < m.year
      OR (m2.year = m.year AND m2.month <= m.month)
  ) AS running_total,
  -- monthly total for same month in previous year
  (SELECT mpy.monthly_total
   FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS mpy
   WHERE mpy.year = m.year - 1
     AND mpy.month = m.month
   LIMIT 1
  ) AS monthly_total_prev_year,
  -- running total up to same month in previous year
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS m2
   WHERE m2.year < m.year - 1
      OR (m2.year = m.year - 1 AND m2.month <= m.month)
  ) AS running_total_prev_year
FROM monthly_city_counts_by_year_month AS m
)
SELECT
  year,
  month_name AS month,
  monthly_total,
  running_total,
  CASE
    WHEN monthly_total_prev_year IS NULL OR monthly_total_prev_year = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0 * (monthly_total - monthly_total_prev_year) / monthly_total_prev_year
  END AS monthly_total_yoy_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN running_total_prev_year IS NULL OR running_total_prev_year = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0 * (running_total - running_total_prev_year) / running_total_prev_year
  END AS running_total_yoy_pct
FROM monthly_running_totals_and_yoy_inputs
WHERE year IN (2022, 2023)
  AND month IN (4, 5, 6)
ORDER BY year ASC, month ASC
